subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw actively recommend Slack HTTP Request URLs for hosted deployments with public ingress, or is the current neutral transport-choice documentation sufficient?
rationale: Current code and docs already support both transports, but changing the recommendation affects setup defaults, operator expectations, and the tradeoff between local Socket Mode convenience and hosted latency/scaling behavior.

options.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted Slack
options.body: Update Slack setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted/public-ingress deployments while keeping Socket Mode as the local/private-ingress default.

options.title: Keep neutral guidance
options.body: Leave the current deployment-shape table as the product stance and close only after recording that no stronger latency recommendation is wanted.

options.title: Defer to setup UX
options.body: Keep the issue open until Slack setup or doctor can surface the transport tradeoff interactively instead of relying on docs alone.

recommendation.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted Slack
recommendation.body: Update Slack setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted/public-ingress deployments while keeping Socket Mode as the local/private-ingress default.

likelyOwner.reason: They produced the measured Slack latency decomposition and merged the OpenClaw-controlled fixes that left this transport-guidance follow-up open.
